failures.criterion: Architect item 2: when whoami answers 503 EVENT_HEAD_UNAVAILABLE rather than 0, the web app retries and resumes, never a broken page or a replay from 0.
failures.evidence: Real Chromium against envoy-dispatch built at dc1fe429 and serving packages/dispatch/web/dist built at the same head. Steps: an event insert (psql, Broker-shaped: xid, owner row, insert) open since before boot and held 15 s; restart; the page opened at once. The page answered whoami 503, 503, 503 (two seconds each) and then showed 'Couldn't reach Dispatch.' with a Retry button. Ten seconds after the insert committed it still showed that message. Only a click on Retry loaded the Inbox, with the fourth whoami answering 200. Main 1f5b0828, same steps: one whoami 200 and the Inbox at once. Without a browser (adv.py whoami503 head 3|6|12 on 5M ids): an insert held 3 s gave 503 at 2.1 s, then 200 at 3.2 s; 6 s gave 503, 503, then 200 at 6.1 s; 12 s gave four 503s through 9.9 s, then 200 at 12.0 s. The web app stops after its third try (main.tsx: retry while failureCount < 2, 500 ms apart), about 7.3 s after the restart, so any such insert held longer than that leaves every page loading then on the error until a click. EVENT_HEAD_UNAVAILABLE already existed on main for a failed read, with the message 'ask again'; this change makes it answer for as long as such a write stays open. Red test e0b2e7f4: 'a page asks whoami again while it answers EVENT_HEAD_UNAVAILABLE, and opens once it answers' in packages/dispatch/e2e/shell.e2e.ts. It stubs whoami to that 503 for 12 s, then lets it through, and expects 'Signed in as alice' within 30 s with no click. Command: cd packages/dispatch && DATABASE_URL=postgres://postgres@127.0.0.1:16432/dispatch_e2e?sslmode=disable PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=<browsers> bun e2e/run.ts -- bunx playwright test --config e2e/playwright.config.ts e2e/shell.e2e.ts -g 'EVENT_HEAD_UNAVAILABLE|a transient whoami failure' --project=chromium. At the head: 1 failed (line 83, 'Signed in as alice' not visible), and the existing transient-failure test passed. Control, reverted: whoAmIQuery retrying while the code is EVENT_HEAD_UNAVAILABLE, with the web app rebuilt, made both pass. The fix is the implementer's to choose. The only caller of /auth/whoami is the web app (useIsHuman and AuthGate share the one query).

proof.criterion: Architect item 1: a mark counts unless a transaction holds a write lock on events; a write that took its xid before boot and inserts only after the first start is still delivered, once, in order.
proof.surface: /ws/live cold subscription on a newly started head process, 5,000,122 ids
proof.observed: The write took its xid and locked its owner row before boot, and did not insert. After the restart the cold subscription started at since=5000122. A comment h=5000123 committed, then the write inserted and committed g=5000124. The subscription received [5000123, 5000124]: each once, in id order. No full-read warning: the write held no lock on events at the start, so the boot mark counted. Its id was drawn after that mark and stands above it, which is what the rule rests on.
proof.negativeControl: Main 1f5b0828 (rounds 11 and 12, same driver): an open lower id was skipped (124 sent, 123 never).

proof.criterion: Architect item 3: the first start on 5M events with a 3 s pre-boot writer, and every event committed during the wait received.
proof.surface: /ws/live on a newly started head process, 5,000,122 ids
proof.command: adv.py wboot head; adv.py bigload head 3.0 0.5 (twice), 3.0 5
proof.observed: An insert open since before boot, a comment h committed 1 s after the cold subscription, then the insert g committed. The full-read warning was logged (as designed: an insert open since before every mark), events_start came 1.36 s after g's commit with since=5000124, and g=5000125, h=5000126 and a later k=5000127 all arrived. Four overlapping inserting writers, each 3 s, subscription 0.5 s after /healthz: full read, events_start 6.03 and 6.20 s after subscribe, the next event delivered. Subscription 5 s after /healthz: no full read, 3.14 s. Round 12's red test now passes, and so does my cold red test, whose writer holds an xid only. The cost of the insert-across-boot case is the round-11 figure, about 3 s on 5M ids: the design reads the whole log rather than lose events. That trade-off is the architect's.
proof.negativeControl: Round 12's head 28d06c20, same wboot steps: events_start since=5000212, and g and h were never sent.
